slides.headline: He thinks he has found true love. Look again.
slides.sub: Frank Dicksee, La Belle Dame sans Merci, 1902

slides.headline: The poem
slides.text: A poem by John Keats: a knight meets a beautiful woman in the meadows and falls in love with her at first sight.

slides.headline: The lady
slides.text: She leans down from his own horse, her red hair falling over him. She has chosen him. Or has she?

slides.headline: The knight
slides.text: He gazes up at her, completely lost, one arm stretched out behind him as if he were falling backwards.

slides.headline: The reins
slides.text: Look at her hands: she is holding the reins of his horse. Now she leads him wherever she wants to go.

slides.headline: The horse
slides.text: Even his mighty warhorse lowers its head, as if it too has already fallen under her strange spell.

slides.headline: The roses
slides.text: Wild roses grow all around them, sweet and thorny at once. Dicksee hides the danger in plain sight.

slides.headline: The warning
slides.text: In Keats's poem, the knight wakes alone on a cold hillside. Pale kings warn him that she has trapped them too.

slides.headline: Follow her?
slides.text: Beautiful, mysterious and without mercy, as the title says. Would you climb down from your horse and follow her?
